prompt: The query in the editor has one mistake. Fix it so that it answers this question: for every order of the customers with customer_id from 3001 to 3100 (both included) placed from 1 January to 30 June 2025 (order_ts holds UTC time; both days included, in UTC), what was the channel of the customer's last order in that period? When two orders of a customer tie on order_ts, the one with the higher order_id counts as the later order. Return four columns, in this order: customer_id, order_id, channel and last_channel. Return one row for each such order. Any row order is fine.
hints: Next, run the query and compare last_channel with channel: on every row they match, because the window stops at the row itself.
With an ORDER BY and no frame, a window ends at the current row; write a frame that reaches the customer's last order.
starter_sql:
SELECT customer_id, order_id, channel,
       LAST_VALUE(channel) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_ts, order_id) AS last_channel
FROM orders
WHERE customer_id BETWEEN 3001 AND 3100
  AND order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01' AND order_ts < TIMESTAMP '2025-07-01'
why_this_works: The written frame runs to the customer's last order, so LAST_VALUE returns that order's channel on every row instead of the row's own.
